items.description: Valentin has the village posters printed, order placed at the printer's on Monday, corrected from Friday because the printer is closed on Friday; asked by Inès and accepted by Valentin.
items.notes: One commitment corrected in place by its owner; Friday is no longer the day. Original statement at turn 4; change at turn 22, 18 turns later.

items.description: Call the tuner for the church piano: Inès asked Oscar, who declined by saying his calendar is full and the tuner never calls back; nobody owns it.
items.notes: The refusal is indirect (full calendar, tuner unreachable).

items.description: Declare the program to the copyright society before November 20, otherwise the concert is not covered; nobody took it on.
items.notes: Obligation stated by Valentin without any owner.

items.description: Inès calls the insurer on Monday morning to get the parish certificate, after nobody answered her open call.
items.notes: Open call at turn 8, silence, then Inès takes it herself at turn 9.

items.description: Collective decision: close the concert with the children's choir alone instead of an audience carol.
items.notes: Counter-proposal by Valentin at turn 11, put to the group at turn 12 and approved by Oscar and Valentin.

items.description: Oscar's proposal of an audience carol with printed scores was rejected (three hundred scores, poor lighting) and dropped in favour of the children's choir.
items.notes: Reporting it as dropped inside the adopted decision (E5) is acceptable; reporting the carol as adopted is not.

items.description: Oscar may take care of the altar flowers if he finishes his moving boxes, with no promise.
Run the refreshment stand on concert night: Inès reported Valentin claiming it, then asked him, and he declined because he is at the sound desk; nobody owns it.
items.notes: The quoted first-person promise at turn 16 is never confirmed by Valentin, who refuses at turn 21.

items.description: Maëlle, absent, will draw up the list of soloists by Wednesday, according to Oscar.
items.notes: Maëlle does not speak in the meeting, so her commitment is only reported.

items.description: Bring the folding chairs back from the community hall on Saturday morning: promised by an unidentified voice, so the owner cannot be confirmed.
items.notes: Nothing identifies the voice as Inès, Valentin or Oscar.

items.description: Valentin prepares the printed program for the concert night and sends it to Inès on Thursday; asked by Inès and accepted by Valentin in the same turn where he refuses the stand.

forbidden.description: No task, for anyone, to call the piano tuner.
No task, for anyone, to declare the program to the copyright society.
No task, for anyone, to run the refreshment stand.
No task, for anyone, to bring back the folding chairs.
No firm task owned by Oscar for the altar flowers.
No firm task owned by Maëlle for the list of soloists.
The audience carol is not a collective decision.
The November 14 meeting is not a task for anyone.

forbidden_claims: Valentin places the poster order on Friday.
Oscar will call the piano tuner.
Inès, Valentin or Oscar brings back the folding chairs.
Oscar will do the altar flowers.
The concert ends with an audience carol.
Maëlle has committed in the meeting to the list of soloists.
A calendar date (day number or month) is given for the Monday, Thursday, Wednesday or Saturday deadlines.
detail_checks: Christmas concert of the choir at the Saint-Aubin church on December 12, forty-two singers.
Parish hall free for a dress rehearsal on December 5.
Sixty posters for the village shops; the printer is closed on Friday.
The parish wants an insurance certificate before mid-November.
Program to be declared to the copyright society before November 20.
Audience carol dropped because of three hundred scores to print and poor lighting.
Valentin cannot run the stand because he is at the sound desk during the concert.
